exercises.title: Hello, World
exercises.prompt:
Write a C program that prints exactly: Hello, World!
(then a newline). It takes no input.

exercises.title: Sum of two integers
exercises.prompt: Read two integers a and b from stdin (space or newline separated) and print their sum on one line.

exercises.title: Even or odd
exercises.prompt: Read one integer n and print the word even if it is even, or odd if it is odd. Print exactly that word on one line.

exercises.title: Factorial
exercises.prompt: Read a non-negative integer n (0 <= n <= 12) and print n! (n factorial) on one line. Recall 0! = 1.

exercises.title: Maximum of three
exercises.prompt: Read three integers and print the largest of them on one line.

exercises.title: Swap with pointers
exercises.prompt: Read two integers x and y. Write a function void swap(int *a, int *b) that swaps the values they point to. Use it to swap x and y, then print them space-separated on one line.

exercises.title: Sum an array with pointers
exercises.prompt: Read an integer n, then read n integers. Store them in a dynamically allocated array (malloc). Compute their sum by traversing the array using pointer arithmetic (e.g. *(a+i)), print the sum on one line, and free the memory.

exercises.title: A Counter class
exercises.prompt: Define a C++ class Counter with a private int member starting at 0, a public method inc() that adds 1, and a public method get() that returns the value. In main, read an integer n, create a Counter, call inc() n times, and print get() on one line.

exercises.title: Inheritance: Animal and Dog
exercises.prompt: Define a base class Animal with a public virtual function string sound() const returning "...". Define a derived class Dog : public Animal that overrides sound() to return "Woof". In main, read a string name, create a Dog, and print exactly: Dog <name> says Woof on one line.
